title: Changes of State
summary: Melting, boiling, evaporation, condensation, freezing and sublimation, and why the temperature stops rising while a substance changes state.

ib.note: Heating curves and energy explanations are extended in MYP 3

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 7: Particulate Nature of Matter
Earlier NCERT: Matter in Our Surroundings (latent heat, evaporation; not in Exploration 2026)

objectives: I can name and describe the six changes of state.
I can read a heating curve and explain why the temperature stays constant during melting and boiling.
I can compare evaporation and boiling, and list factors that speed up evaporation.
I can convert between degrees Celsius and kelvin.
misconceptions: The bubbles in boiling water are air.
The temperature keeps rising steadily while ice melts.
Steam is the white cloud you see above a kettle (that is tiny droplets of liquid water).
